status: Complete evidence-guided attribution, not surveyed building counts
interpretation: Coefficients are explicit shared attribution assumptions, not historical measured percentages. Freeze before examining capacity outcomes; test half and one-and-a-half transfer strength.

GLWD 1990-2020 and 1700 wetland reconstruction characterize physical settings, not infrastructure existing in 1300. HYDE/LUH cultivation and existing Seshat-guided crop/system assignments determine the inherited-budget context.
Wet-rice control is distinguished from supplementary water supply: bunded rainfed rice also requires control. Modern rice does not authorize a historically unavailable crop.
The modern and 1700 wetland layers are combined with max rather than added; overlapping paddy, polder, flood and drainage settings are partitioned once in that order.

No new capacity, water withdrawal, physical hectares, groundwater or seasonal storage is created. Starting and maximum total support remain unchanged. Evidenced water-dependent cultivation may move from base to starting and maximum works, retaining natural livelihood support and the game base floor.

Reservoirs and qanats are not separate chosen categories; their independently quantified opportunity is outside the present surface-water model. No zero-filled placeholder maps masquerade as those estimates.

Already reclaimed coastal land can be absent from modern and 1700 wetland inventories. Fine ETOPO subcells between -10 and 0m within the low coastal screen identify an inferred drainage/reclamation dependency; this is not a date of construction.

Base transfers require reconstructed cultivation overlapping baseline-access cropland, the positive crop-over-livelihood support share, and an exclusive paddy/drainage/coastal setting. No base transfer for natural floodplain wetness or water-supply scenarios. Base-dependency coefficients are shared scenario assumptions, not observed historical percentages.
